issue: Does attempted bank robbery under 18 U.S.C. § 2113(a) require proof of force, violence, or intimidation, given that the phrase 'by force and violence, or by intimidation' may modify only 'takes' and not 'attempts to take'?

sides.position: Attempted bank robbery under § 2113(a) requires force or intimidation, so the adverbial phrase also modifies 'attempts to take'.
cases: Collier v. United States, 989 F.3d 212, 221 (2d Cir. 2021)
United States v. Bellew, 369 F.3d 450, 454 (5th Cir. 2004)
United States v. Thornton, 539 F.3d 741, 747 (7th Cir. 2008)
United States v. Vines, 134 F.4th 730 (3d Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Attempted bank robbery under § 2113(a) does not require force, violence, or intimidation.
cases: United States v. McFadden, 739 F.2d 149, 151-52 (4th Cir. 1984)
United States v. Wesley, 417 F.3d 612, 618 (6th Cir. 2005)
United States v. Moore, 921 F.2d 207, 209 (9th Cir. 1990)

this_court: requires force or intimidation. The excerpt does not state the holding on this split in so many words, but the court reasons that a § 2113(d) attempt must incorporate § 2113(a)'s elements, which make it a crime of violence.
